name: Thebes
note: Kadmos and Harmonia, and the house that could not stop killing itself

people.Agenor: Twin of Belos; he went to Phoenicia and became king of Tyre, and when Zeus took his daughter Europa he sent his sons after her with orders not to come back without her. None of them did come back, and each founded a country looking. Apollod. 2.1.4, 3.1.1

Deianeira.note: Herakles' last wife, who sent him the shirt smeared with the centaur Nessos' blood believing it a love-charm; it burned him alive and he built his own pyre. Apollod. 2.7.5-7

people.Kadmos: Sent after his sister Europa and told not to come home without her; the oracle instead told him to follow a cow and found a city where she lay down. He killed the dragon at the spring, sowed its teeth, and the Sown Men who came up fought each other until five were left, who became the Theban nobility. Greek tradition credits him with bringing the ALPHABET from Phoenicia -- which is true, and the letters are still called Kadmeian. Apollod. 3.1.1, 3.4.1-2

Harmonia.note: Daughter of Ares and Aphrodite -- war and love -- given to Kadmos, and the first mortal wedding all the gods attended. Her necklace, made by Hephaistos, brought disaster to every woman who wore it for six generations. Apollod. 3.4.2

Semele.note: Loved by Zeus, and tricked by Hera into asking to see him as he appears to Hera -- the lightning burned her up, and Zeus sewed the six-month child into his own thigh to finish it. Apollod. 3.4.3

Ino.note: Sister of Semele who nursed Dionysos, was driven mad by Hera, and leapt into the sea to become the goddess Leukothea, who saves drowning sailors -- she gives Odysseus her veil. Apollod. 3.4.3, Od. 5.333-353

Agaue.note: Sister of Semele who, maddened in the Bacchic rites, tore her own son Pentheus apart believing him a lion. Apollod. 3.5.2, Euripides Bacchae

Autonoe.note: Sister of Semele and mother of Aktaion. Apollod. 3.4.4

people.Polydoros: Son of Kadmos and Harmonia, and the one through whom the throne descends. Apollod. 3.4.2, 3.5.5
people.Pentheus: King of Thebes who refused the new god and was torn apart by his own mother and aunts on Kithairon. Euripides Bacchae; Apollod. 3.5.2
people.Aktaion: Saw Artemis bathing, was turned into a stag, and was eaten by his own fifty hounds. Apollod. 3.4.4
people.Labdakos: Son of Polydoros, and the man the house is named for: the Labdakidai. Apollod. 3.5.5
people.Laios: King of Thebes, told by the oracle that his own son would kill him. He pinned the baby's ankles and left him on the mountain, and was killed by him anyway at a crossroads twenty years later in a quarrel about right of way. Apollod. 3.5.7-8 Before any of it he carried off Chrysippos, son of Pelops, while a guest in his house; Pelops' curse on him for it is the first cause of everything the Labdakidai suffer.

Iokaste.name: Iokaste (Jocasta)
Iokaste.note: Wife of Laios and then, unknowingly, of her own son; she hanged herself when she understood. Apollod. 3.5.7-9, Sophocles OT

Oidipous.name: Oidipous (Oedipus)
Oidipous.note: Swollen-foot, from the pin through his ankles. He answered the Sphinx's riddle, won Thebes and its widowed queen, and spent the play finding out that the murderer he had sworn to hunt was himself. Blinded himself with her brooches. Freud took the name in 1899 for the complex, which has made him the best-known Greek in English and the least accurately remembered. Apollod. 3.5.7-9, Sophocles OT

Eteokles.note: Son of Oidipous, who refused to give up the throne in his brother's year and died on his spear as his brother died on his. Apollod. 3.6.1-8, Aeschylus Seven

Polyneikes.note: Son of Oidipous, who brought the Seven against his own city to take his turn at the throne. His unburied body is the whole argument of the Antigone. Apollod. 3.6.1-8

Antigone.note: Daughter of Oidipous, who buried her brother against the king's express order and was walled up alive for it -- the oldest statement in Europe that there is a law above the state's. Sophocles Antigone; Apollod. 3.7.1

Ismene.note: Her sister, who would not help her and lived. Sophocles Antigone

Teiresias.note: The blind prophet of Thebes, who lived seven generations, was a woman for seven years, and was asked by Zeus and Hera which sex enjoys love more -- he answered, and Hera blinded him, and Zeus gave him prophecy in exchange. Od. 11.90-151, Apollod. 3.6.7

Antiope.note: Loved by Zeus as a satyr, and imprisoned by her uncle; she bore twins on the mountain and they came back grown to take Thebes. Apollod. 3.5.5

Amphion.note: Twin son of Antiope, who built the walls of Thebes by playing his lyre until the stones came and laid themselves. Married Niobe, and watched Apollo and Artemis shoot all fourteen of their children. Apollod. 3.5.5-6

Zethos.note: His twin, who carried the stones by hand and thought his brother's music was idleness. Apollod. 3.5.5

Megara.note: Herakles' first wife, given him by the king of Thebes. Hera sent him mad and he killed her and their children with his own hands, and the twelve labours are the penance for it. Apollod. 2.4.11-12

unions.note: Their mother is Iokaste, who is also his own; the marriage stands beside this as a cross-era bond, because the children's generation has to come from a parent the leveller can see. Apollod. 3.5.8-9
Standing free of the royal line; his place is the city, not the house.
Fourteen children, all shot in one afternoon for their mother's boast. Il. 24.602-617
And then, at Hera's prompting, she asked to see him as Hera sees him. Apollod. 3.4.3
He came to her as a satyr; she was imprisoned by her uncle for the pregnancy. Apollod. 3.5.5

Carried off while Laios was a guest in his father's house: the act the tradition names as the first pederasty, and the reason Pelops cursed the house of Laios. Everything Oidipous suffers begins here. Apollod. 3.5.5, Hyg. Fab. 85
Mother and wife. Their four children hang from him, not from this bond, because a generation must come from a parent the leveller can see. Apollod. 3.5.8-9
